## Overview

WeChat Pay is the wallet inside Tencent's WeChat app. The November 7, 2026 overview describes single-use B2C payments with immediate confirmation timing and a standard payout schedule. The May 8, 2026 capture describes Chinese consumers, overseas Chinese and travelers and reports over 800 million wallet users and over 1 billion monthly active users for WeChat. Those figures are historical. See November lines 9–14 and May lines 8–24.

## Account and payment eligibility

The November method overview lists CN customer location, domestic and cross-border coverage and a minimum amount of USD 0.50. It retains the 22 Stripe account locations AT, AU, BE, CA, CH, DE, DK, ES, FI, FR, GB, HK, IE, IT, JP, LU, NL, NO, PT, SE, SG and US, with country-mapped presentment in AUD, CAD, CHF, CNY, DKK, EUR, GBP, HKD, JPY, NOK, SEK, SGD or USD. CNY is available for all listed account countries and is what the buyer sees. The separate May Checkout acceptance example lists 35 business codes for that documented path. See November lines 18–21 and 36–71, May lines 57–83 and 125–143, and [[source-stripe-wechat-pay-accept-payment]].

November labels access “Instant provisional access” for eligible merchants and Connect platforms or marketplaces. Businesses must comply with both Stripe's restricted-business rules and WeChat Pay's Proper Use Rules. The merchant needs an operational website accessible for review, with products or services, prices and working checkout. Its business information must match the information provided to Stripe. A social profile alone is insufficient. If acceptance is restricted or disabled and the merchant believes the decision is incorrect, Stripe Support can review it. Complete requested changes or provide requested information and reply to the notification. Reinstatement depends on that review, which is separate from preview registration. See November lines 12 and 18–34.

## Checkout, native payments and previews

The November method guide recommends full-page Checkout and Checkout Sessions. It also lists Payment Links, embedded Checkout, Payment Element, PaymentIntents, Invoicing (`send_invoice` only), Radar, Connect and Terminal outside Japan. The Dashboard can enable dynamic display and separate manual configuration is available, including the Terminal smart-reader flow. Checkout excludes subscription and setup modes. Express Checkout Element and the general in-app product label are unsupported, and the cross-method matrix marks Mobile Payment Element unsupported. The November acceptance index links Checkout, Direct API, iOS and Android without their instructions. See November lines 152–181 and 225–237 and [[source-stripe-wechat-pay-accept-payment]].

On desktop the customer scans the QR code and authorizes in WeChat. Checkout stays on the QR screen and the authorization window is two hours from payment-request creation. On expiry the customer starts another attempt. In a supported native integration the merchant app opens WeChat Pay, and the customer returns to the merchant app after authorization. Stripe-hosted instructions show success and amount paid after a successful payment. In a custom or native flow the merchant's server confirms `PaymentIntent.status` is `succeeded` before showing success. Application return, payment confirmation and payout have separate meanings. See November lines 183–203.

The November general capabilities and API lists exclude recurring payments, SetupIntents, `setup_future_usage` and off-session payments. The same guide describes an independently requested private preview for off-session-only recurring payments and another private preview for mini-program payments. The [November cross-method matrix](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/payment-method-support) lists private preview for Subscriptions with `send_invoice`, SetupIntents and future usage, and its redirect cell says Yes. May's matrix lists supported Subscriptions with `send_invoice`, unsupported SetupIntents and future usage, and a redirect cell of No. The May product matrix lists Terminal N/A, while the November matrix lists Terminal outside Japan, the boundary already documented in both method overviews. These matrix labels describe dated product and API scope. The QR and native flows above supply the method-specific behavior. See November lines 73–74, 118–177 and [[source-stripe-payment-method-support]].

## Refunds and disputes

Full and partial refunds are asynchronous and can be requested within 180 days of the original payment. Stripe processes same-day requests immediately and later requests in a daily noon UTC+8 batch. Linked-card receipt can take another two to five days. Refunds cannot be canceled. WeChat returns funds to the original source, such as WeChat balance or a linked payment method, through a refund rather than a reversal. Track the Refund status and final `refund.updated` or `refund.failed` event. A failure returns funds to the merchant's Stripe balance and requires an alternative refund method. See November lines 89–110 and May lines 120–123.

The November guide excludes manual, partial, multiple and over-capture and its listed extended or adjusted authorization types. WeChat Pay has no standard dispute or chargeback process, with in-app authorization required. WeChat may refer customer payment complaints back to the merchant, who can then issue a refund. See November lines 73–97 and 112–116 and May lines 45–55 and 116–118.

## Connect, statement descriptions and reconciliation

Destination charges and separate charges and transfers are generally available. Direct charges and `on_behalf_of` require private-preview access. A connected account with standard Dashboard access can enable the method itself. For other connected accounts the platform requests `capabilities.wechat_pay_payments.requested`, with the capability in private preview. See November lines 176–177 and 231–237 and May lines 145–161.

Stripe sends WeChat the settlement merchant's business name, the text `online` and the payment's statement descriptor. The account supplying the business name depends on the charge.

| Charge | Business name in WeChat order information |
| --- | --- |
| Destination without `on_behalf_of` | Platform account |
| Destination with `on_behalf_of` | Specified connected account |
| Direct | Connected account on which the payment was created |

The buyer-visible registered merchant name and linked bank or card statement can differ from the order information. For reconciliation, retrieve the PaymentIntent, expand `latest_charge` and read `latest_charge.payment_method_details.wechat_pay.transaction_id`. See November lines 205–223.

payments-wechat-pay.text: A social media profile alone doesn’t qualify as your business website.
You can’t cancel WeChat Pay refunds.
Recurring WeChat Pay payments are in private preview and support off-session use only.
For the desktop QR-code flow, customers must complete authorization within two hours after the payment request is created.
Payments made with WeChat Pay can only be submitted for refund within 180 days from the date of the original charge.

payments-wechat-pay.Q1: The 2026-11-07 full capture at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/wechat-pay documents a wallet whose eligible B2C merchant enables WeChat Pay, with a working business website and applicable restrictions, and whose Chinese customer authorizes in the WeChat app. New raw lines 9-55, 73-150 and 152-237 distinguish desktop QR authorization within two hours from eligible native-mobile return, server-confirmed PaymentIntent success and standard payout. It retains the old 22 merchant locations, account-mapped currencies, no manual capture or chargeback and asynchronous refunds in old raw lines 8-161, and adds refund timing, noncancellation, two separately gated previews, and Connect descriptor and reconciliation details. source-stripe-wechat-pay.md now dates the May behavior and records the November eligibility, preview and operational boundaries.
payments-wechat-pay.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/wechat-pay, old raw lines 8-161 and new raw lines 9-237 separate reorganization and navigation from substantive additions such as Stripe/WeChat restrictions, reviewable website and conditional reinstatement review, refund batch/receipt timing, two-hour desktop expiry, Connect descriptors and reconciliation, and off-session recurring and mini-program previews. Preserve November's general unsupported recurring/setup/off-session labels alongside the distinct gated preview prose and API matrix. The cross-method tables change the dated Subscriptions label from supported send_invoice to private preview send_invoice, Terminal from N/A to supported outside Japan, and SetupIntents and future usage from unsupported to private preview. The API matrix redirect label changes from No to Yes. The separate acceptance index links Checkout, Direct API, iOS and Android. Preserve the overview's 22 markets versus the separate 35-code May Checkout eligibility list, and distinguish supported native flows from the Mobile Payment Element restriction. Terminal outside Japan appears in both method overviews. source-stripe-wechat-pay.md retains both full dated captures, links the separate acceptance and matrix routes, and links back to the Wallets concept. The Stripe provider index continues to route to both source guides.

concept_suggestions.anchor:
**Chinese consumers, overseas Chinese, and Chinese travelers**. Part of WeChat super app (1B+ MAU); WeChat Pay has 800M+ users. Top verticals: gaming, e-commerce, travel, online education, food, nutrition.

**13 presentment currencies**: CNY (default, always shown to customer) + AUD, CAD, EUR, GBP, HKD, JPY, SGD, USD, DKK, NOK, SEK, CHF — mapped by merchant country.

**22 merchant countries** (AT, AU, BE, CA, CH, DE, DK, ES, FI, FR, GB, HK, IE, IT, JP, LU, NL, NO, PT, SE, SG, US).

**No recurring. No manual capture. No disputes** — customer authenticates in WeChat app, low fraud risk, no chargeback process.

**Refunds**: full + partial, 180-day window, async. Failed refunds return to Stripe balance.
concept_suggestions.proposed_markdown:
**Dated WeChat Pay overview.** May 2026 describes Chinese consumers, overseas Chinese and travelers, with more than 800 million wallet users and more than 1 billion WeChat monthly active users. November lists B2C, CN customer location, 22 Stripe account locations (AT, AU, BE, CA, CH, DE, DK, ES, FI, FR, GB, HK, IE, IT, JP, LU, NL, NO, PT, SE, SG and US), domestic and cross-border payments and account-mapped presentment. CNY is available in all those account locations and is the amount shown to the buyer. Eligibility includes a working website accessible for review and both providers' business rules.

**November capabilities.** Single use in the general overview, with independently gated off-session recurring and mini-program private previews. General Checkout continues to exclude setup and subscription modes. The method has no manual capture or standard chargebacks. Full and partial refunds are asynchronous and noncancelable, within 180 days of payment. Failed refunds return to the Stripe balance. See [[source-stripe-wechat-pay]] for the dated matrix, authorization, refund and Connect details.
warnings: November raw lines 9–71, 73–150 and 152–237 supply the method and preview scopes. May raw lines 8–24, 33–55 and 57–83 establish the older audience and general labels. The separate Checkout integration count is owned by the acceptance route.
